PullRequest.Title: sessions: add rich GitHub reference previews
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Exploratory follow-up to #335448, building on the first-level title work from #335387.

This proposal adds a compact issue/PR preview to Agents Window reference pills so users can identify a GitHub object and decide whether to open it without leaving their current context.

## Design rationale

- **Progressive disclosure:** collections keep the existing scannable list; focusing a row reveals detail. A single reference shows the same detail directly.
- **Source-product hierarchy:** GitHub's own hover cards inform the order of information, while VS Code continues to own typography, color, spacing, popup chrome, focus, and keyboard behavior. Collection rows lead with the lifecycle icon, followed by the canonical title and a muted trailing ID.
- **Bounded transient content:** the card provides identity and enough context to make a decision, rather than becoming a full issue reader.
- **Consistent information budget:** standalone and collection cards contain the same information; only their outer density differs.

The resulting card order is repository/date → title/ID → lifecycle and CI state → bounded description → PR branches → author. Open and draft pull requests show the shared overall checks state as `Checks pending`, `Checks failed`, or `Checks passed`; closed, merged, and no-check states stay quiet. Pending uses GitHub's familiar attention-colored static dot rather than a spinner or sync metaphor because the aggregate may include both queued and running checks. Both status pills use neutral text and surfaces, while their icons carry restrained semantic color.

Descriptions are normalized from Markdown and bounded to 200 Unicode code points. Visible titles are bounded to 80 Unicode code points. The final visible title word and linked ID are grouped so the number cannot interrupt the sentence or become clipped at narrow widths.

#335448 also explores a full Markdown reader across broader GitHub-reference surfaces; this iteration focuses on the compact pill-hover treatment.

## What inspired the design

- **GitHub hover cards:** provenance first, title and ID as the lead, state next, then context, routing details, and authorship/viewer context.
- **GitLab and GitHub PR experiences:** emphasize identity, state, and short context before secondary metadata.
- **Linear/Slack unfurls:** keep transient previews concise and action-oriented instead of reproducing the full work item.
- **JetBrains and VS Code GitHub PR lists:** use an overall checks result in compact references, while reserving individual checks, review state, and denser metadata for persistent triage surfaces.
- **Existing VS Code patterns:** reuse the issue/PR hover components, ActionList list/dialog semantics, SessionSummaryHover hierarchy, branch pills, popup chrome, focus indicators, and spacing tokens.

Those examples drove the current boundary: enough content to understand and route the reference, with individual checks, labels, reactions, comments, assignees, and full Markdown left to richer or persistent surfaces.

## Collection item interactions

### Pull request collection

The clip follows the complete reverse Shift+Tab sequence back through every card control and row action.

### Issue collection

## Single-reference interactions

A single reference skips the list but keeps the same information budget.

### Single pull request

![Single pull request chip expanded with its rich preview showing draft and checks-pending status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4842658c-f51d-470d-ba5d-cda15e140368)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cf5da59b-2bfd-4add-9a31-a92c4586a9f9

Uses Shift+Tab and ArrowRight to focus the direct PR chip, then opens its hover with the live overall CI result and moves through repository, linked ID, and base/head branch controls.

### Single issue

![Single issue chip expanded with its rich issue preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48e07143-9e6b-4479-8e69-6b27b41a81ec)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26ef0069-4969-4151-8ae2-cbc6cd7f1b32

Uses Shift+Tab and ArrowRight to focus the direct issue chip, then opens its hover and moves through repository and linked ID.

## Keyboard and screen-reader behavior

- **Collections:** Shift+Tab from the chat input focuses the first pill; Left/Right moves between pills.
- **Collections:** Enter/Space opens the list, Up/Down moves through rows, and the metadata card follows the focused item.
- **Collections:** Tab moves through Copy URL, repository, resource ID, and PR branch controls; Shift+Tab returns to Copy URL.
- **Single references:** Enter/Space activates the reference directly; pointer hover exposes the same detail content and its links/branch controls.
- The listbox retains keyboard focus while the named detail dialog remains available in screen-reader reading order.
- Rows announce the full resource title, lifecycle state, and overall CI result. The detail card reads provenance → title/ID → lifecycle/CI state → description → branches → author.
- Focusing a bounded title's ID reveals the full canonical title; blur restores the compact title.

## Implementation

- reuses `ChatDropdownPillActionViewItem`, `ActionListWidget`, `createIssueHoverElement`, and `createPullRequestHoverElement`
- keeps standalone and collection content identical
- reads the existing shared CI model; no additional GitHub request path is introduced
- polls CI for open pull requests, including drafts, while keeping review-thread icon refinement limited to non-drafts
- preserves GitHub's distinct `Duplicate` and `Not planned` issue terminology
- makes ActionList and managed-hover padding ownership explicit instead of using compensating offsets
- uses standard ActionWidget border, radius, background, shadow, and spacing tokens
- uses measured panel dimensions for viewport positioning

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint and stylelint
- focused ActionList and Sessions toolbar tests: 103 passing
- dark/light and keyboard-focus fixtures
- standalone issue and PR paths
- live Open, Draft, Closed, Merged, Completed, and Not planned resources
- live draft PR with pending checks; unit coverage for pending, passing, failing, and no-check states
- 567-character title and 300px-width stress cases
- linked ID remains fully visible and focusing it does not scroll clipped content

## Related VS Code TPI

This work is tracked by [#337045](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337045), which covers rich previews for issue and pull-request collections in the regular editor window. The original rich-metadata issue is [#335448](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335448), and reference accumulation/removal is tracked by [#336500](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/336500).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed guard, all-session ownership, exact REST endpoint, shared-key coalescing, and 60-second cadence are directly traced. Only the number of users with multiple unarchived draft PRs is uncertain, which limits severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub HTTP check-runs requests and their response parsing/model updates
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost is one immediate request plus one request per minute for every unique open draft PR head across all unarchived tracked sessions; different drafts start independently with no aggregate limiter.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive network I/O and background CPU, with startup request bursts and reduced GitHub API quota
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous guard returned for open drafts before acquiring or refreshing a CI model, so inactive draft sessions generated no check-runs traffic from this contribution.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The status autorun no longer rejects draft pull requests, so every open draft tracked by the global contribution now creates a CI model, refreshes it immediately, and starts its 60-second poll loop.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 278 removes `prDetails.isDraft` from the early-return condition, making draft PRs flow into the existing refresh/startPolling calls that were previously unreachable for them.
Findings.Title: Keep draft CI polling off the global session path
Findings.Impact: Opening VS Code with accumulated agent sessions containing draft PRs creates an immediate burst of GitHub requests and then continuous background traffic even if the user never opens a reference hover, increasing network/battery use and consuming API quota.
Findings.Evidence: GitHubPullRequestPollingContribution tracks every added unarchived session, including non-active sessions, and invokes this autorun for each referenced PR. The now-reachable lines 287-289 call refresh() and startPolling(); GitHubPullRequestCIModel.refresh issues GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs, and its default polling interval is 60,000 ms. Models are shared by owner/repo/PR/head SHA, so duplicate session references coalesce, but each unique draft head retains its own poller.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not keep draft CI warm for every tracked session. Preserve draft hover status by refreshing lazily when its pill/dropdown is actually shown, or restrict recurring draft polling to the active/visible session and dispose it when that visibility ends.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous focus call path and parser/sanitizer implementation are directly traced, and the absence of caching is explicit. Exact milliseconds vary with body shape and hardware, so severity is medium.
Findings.PerformanceResource: main-thread Markdown parsing/sanitization CPU plus transient token, HTML, normalized-string, and Unicode-array allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Work grows with the full body length and the number of focus/hover transitions, while useful output remains capped at 200 code points; repeated visits parse the same body again.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased interaction latency, CPU/GC pressure, and possible dropped frames during list navigation
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Collection rows had no rich detail construction on focus, and standalone hovers inserted the body as text without invoking the Markdown parser/sanitizer. The PR therefore adds full Markdown parsing to this interaction path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Rich issue/PR hovers now run renderAsPlaintext, whitespace normalization, and Unicode-array truncation over the complete body each time hover content is constructed, even though only 200 code points are displayed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 16 introduces full-body `renderAsPlaintext(...)` before line 17 applies the 200-code-point limit; the new dropdown hover factories make this helper run synchronously on focused-row changes.
Findings.Title: Bound Markdown work before building the 200-character preview
Findings.Impact: Keyboarding or hovering through a collection containing long issue templates, logs, or PR descriptions can block the UI thread on each row transition, causing delayed focus updates and dropped frames; revisiting rows repeats the same parse and allocations.
Findings.Evidence: renderAsPlaintext calls marked.parse and sanitizeRenderedMarkdown over up to 100,000 input characters before returning. ActionList.onFocus synchronously calls _showHoverForElement, whose _showSubmenuForElement invokes the entry's hover.content factory; buildSessionIssueSections/buildSessionPullRequestSections create a fresh hover each time, and revisiting a row repeats the work with no memoization.
Findings.Recommendation: Produce the preview with a bounded-input/streaming plain-text extraction that stops after enough visible text, or memoize a bounded normalized preview per immutable body and compute it outside the focus handler, so row navigation only builds the small DOM card.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench restore and ongoing background tracking of agent sessions with open draft pull requests
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The network work is asynchronous and off the immediate UI critical path, but it begins during the AfterRestored contribution and remains active for the lifetime of each unarchived tracked session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For each unique open draft PR head: one immediate refresh, then one request every 60 seconds while any unarchived session retains the key; duplicates coalesce by shared model key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Draft PRs returned before CI model acquisition, refresh, and polling, so this contribution made zero check-runs requests for them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the direct render path, but continuously consumes network/API quota and can burst during restore.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch PR details/reviews to determine live state and head SHA
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing shared per-PR refresh/poll behavior for tracked sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same PR model refresh and polling already ran before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Supplies the state that gates CI polling; asynchronous and unchanged by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unique owner/repository/PR/head-SHA keys for open draft PRs across all unarchived sessions; duplicate references to the same key share one model and poll loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refresh calls coalesce only within one shared CI model via _refreshPromise. Distinct draft-head models schedule independently, with no aggregate network limiter, so restore can start a burst across unique drafts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The reference collection shares positive model state by PR head. Warm polls send an ETag and may receive 304, reducing payload but not request cardinality. There is no visibility gate or negative cache that suppresses polling for unseen draft hovers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all-session ownership, shared-key behavior, exact endpoint, immediate refresh, and 60-second cadence are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of users retaining many simultaneous open drafts is unknown; request cadence and per-key fan-out are fixed and directly evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the broadened guard introduces perpetual background CI traffic for drafts solely to keep optional hover metadata fresh.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a multi-reference issue/PR pill and navigate focused rows with keyboard or pointer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ActionList focus handling synchronously constructs the selected row's detail card before the focus transition/layout completes; Markdown parsing and sanitization are therefore on the interaction critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: marked.parse plus sanitizeRenderedMarkdown, whitespace replacement, Unicode array creation, and truncation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per focused rich row construction and again for each revisit; one operation processes the entire body before retaining 200 code points.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Collection rows had no rich body card and did not parse Markdown on focus.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly blocks focused-row update and detail-panel rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Full issue/PR body length multiplied by focused-row transitions, including revisits. Displayed output is only 200 code points, but input processing is capped much later at 100,000 UTF-16 units.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Strictly serialized on the browser main thread; every focus transition completes its own parsing, sanitization, string normalization, DOM creation, and geometry measurement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved GitHub models provide body data without a new hover-time network request, but normalized previews and DOM cards are not cached. Returning to a row reconstructs and reparses it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the synchronous focus-to-content-factory call path and full-input parser/sanitizer are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact stall duration depends on body shape, hardware, and how often users navigate references; long templates/logs are realistic but prevalence is uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: useful output is bounded after unbounded synchronous work, and identical work repeats on revisits.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show the rich hover for a single issue or pull request pill
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The managed hover content factory constructs the card synchronously when the hover is requested; full-body Markdown normalization must finish before content can display.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse and sanitize the full Markdown body to derive a 200-code-point plaintext preview
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-body operation per hover construction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old hover inserted the raw body as text and did not invoke marked parsing or sanitizer work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One full issue/PR body per hover show, repeated if the managed hover is recreated.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized on the main thread; no worker or deferred computation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Live issue/PR data comes from existing shared models. There is no preview cache, so warm hover shows still repeat body normalization when the factory runs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both old and new hover implementations and the parser implementation were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Single-show cost may be modest for short bodies; degradation grows with long bodies and repeated hover creation.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the synchronous Markdown finding; it reinforces the same changed mechanism rather than requiring a separate issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Tab through a collection row toolbar and rich detail controls, then move between rows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Key handling, focus transfer, panel clearing/reconstruction, and layout measurement are synchronous; no subprocess, filesystem, database, IPC, or network call occurs directly in this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of toolbar/detail controls and row transitions; GitHub cards expose two issue controls or up to four PR controls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single main-thread event sequence. Previous panel DOM is cleared before the next is built, so only the current card remains attached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Toolbar instances are tracked per rendered row and removed through element disposables. Tabbable element arrays retain only each entry's latest card controls; old cards become collectible after replacement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registration, disposal, panel clearing, and key paths were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Layout cost varies by viewport but control counts are small and bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression beyond the full-body work performed during card reconstruction; the new maps/listeners have bounded cleanup ownership.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 32 changed files. Reported two diff-caused regressions: global one-minute CI polling newly applied to draft PRs, and full-body Markdown parsing/sanitization on synchronous rich-hover construction before a 200-code-point cap. Verified shared-model coalescing, request cadence, focus call paths, cache behavior, concurrency, and DOM/listener cleanup; no other high-confidence performance issue or regression-fix learning signal was found.
